summary: Bisheshwar Nath Reu (1890–1966) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha. He headed the Sardar Government Museum and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre, and served as Superintendent of Sumer Public Library's Archæological Department (attested 1933).
Biswajit Biswas works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at the Asiatic Society.
Biswanath Banerjee (born 1926) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (1967–1991) and served as president of the Asiatic Society circa 1999–2001.
Bo Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas (born 1938) is a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Uppsala University (~1958–1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander (~1958–1968), and held a post there circa 1978–2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a scholar of Buddhist studies and a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2004 and 2015). He taught Silwon Suk.

Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989). He served at Bokar Monastery (~1984–2004) and taught Shenpen Hookham, Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö.

Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD at Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser, also studying under Jacqueline I. Stone, Yang Lu, Lewis R. Lancaster, Ding-hwa Hsieh, and Morio Hamada.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Michigan State University under George C. Kerner and held posts at Florida International University, including in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy (attested 2012).

Boris Turayev (1868–1920) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (circa 1887–1891). He taught at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1898–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920), where he instructed Otto Neugebauer and George de Roerich.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (~1920–1925) and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1925–1933).

Boris Vladimirtsov (1884–1931) studied at St. Petersburg University and under Antoine Meillet (1911). He worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history/archaeology, holding posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1915–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).

Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Shrisingha Shedra under Khenchen Thubten Nyendrak and Khenpo Genam. He taught Khenpo Chokhyap, Khenpo Dazer, Jigme Phuntsok, Tarthang Tulku, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje.
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Krzysztof Byrski. She held a faculty post at the University of Warsaw circa 1991.

Bradford Lyman Phillips studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning degrees from Naropa University, the University of Virginia (BA -1989; PhD -2004), and Harvard (MTS -1993). He studied under David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. He held the post of Assistant Director at Boston University and was affiliated with Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Allahabad University and trained under Mortimer Wheeler (1943). He was Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2002–2006) and a habilitation at Munich (~2010–2013), holding posts at SOAS (~2006–2010) and the University of Munich (~2010–2017).
Brandon J. Harwood earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015), where he studied under advisors Patrick Arthur Pranke and John Gibson.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee (1932–2013) studied history and Indology at Calcutta, Cambridge, and SOAS, earning a doctorate under A. L. Basham. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (1975–1998).
